subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive TCO & next tests
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Competitive TCO & next tests

Jordan — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock a short test: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: conversational chat (70% of tokens) + embeddings for search/rerank (30%).
- SLO: p50 latency target ~200ms for chat; embeddings can be higher.
- Primary competitive comps: AWS Bedrock (Titan/Anthropic), Azure OpenAI, and a small on-prem stack for sensitive data.
- Main eval criteria: unit cost (per-1M tokens for gen + per-1M tokens for embeddings), latency, cold/warm cache behavior, and operational controls (routing, fallbacks).

What Redwood will provide (initial)
- Per-1M token cost profiles for hosted + an estimate for Dedicated (reserved) capacity.
- Modeled TCO spreadsheet with batch/caching sensitivity (attached).
- A proposed 48-hour controlled POC to run your sample workload against Redwood and one hyperscaler endpoint so you can compare unit economics and latency.

Requests from your side
- A sample workload (trace or synthetic mix) we can run; attaching the model with placeholders — if you can send a small sample JSON of typical requests that’ll speed things up.
- Any compliance requirements (SOC2, data residency) that we should map to the trial environment.

Attachments:
- redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx (initial cost model)
- comparison-metrics.pdf (example report from prior POC)

Proposed next steps
1) You send sample workload file (or confirm we can use the example mix on tab "workload").
2) We spin up a trial Dedicated instance + hosted API baseline and run a 48h A/B.
3) Sync to review results and discuss contract terms.

Available times for an engineering sync: Mon/Tue next week 10–12 PT.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the spreadsheet while we prepare the POC.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
Attachment: comparison-metrics.pdf (pdf, 95KB)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive TCO & next tests

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items before we kick off the trial: 

1) Workload specifics: the 70/30 split is correct. Typical prompt length for chat is 60 tokens (user) + 120 tokens (assistant) average, and embeddings requests are ~512 tokens.
2) Latency: 200ms p50 is our goal; p95 can be up to 1s for non-critical paths.
3) Caching: we do a lot of prompt reuse across sessions; cache hit rate will materially change unit costs — can you show a few scenarios (0%, 30%, 60% hit) in the model?
4) Hyperscaler comparison: we want to measure Redwood vs AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI (their inference APIs) on both cost and latency. Are there any known model parity issues (e.g., Redwood uses different model variants) that would affect quality?

I attached a small synthetic sample (acme-workload-sample.json) — feel free to use it directly. Also looping in procurement for any paperwork.

If you can send estimated per-1M token numbers (hosted, dedicated estimate, and % improvement from batching/caching) that would be ideal — we’ll use this to build our internal TCO.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acme.com

Attachment: acme-workload-sample.json (json, 8KB)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive TCO & next tests

Jordan — great, thanks for the sample. I updated the model with the three cache-hit scenarios you asked for and ran a few quick sensitivity slices (attached updated workbook). High level answers below — we can go deeper in the POC.

Per-1M token estimates (hosted, generation):
- Redwood hosted (base gen): ~$6.50 per 1M output tokens (est) — includes continuous batching and runtime optimizations.
- Embeddings: ~$4.00 per 1M embedding token-equivalents (note: embeddings billed per request in most hyperscalers; we normalize to per-1M tokens for comparison).

Dedicated / Reserved estimate (normalized):
- Dedicated (reserved pool): effective per-1M generation token unit cost drops to ~$3.50–$4.50 depending on commit and average utilization. The modeled sheet uses 70% utilization for baseline.

Batching & cache impact (examples):
- Batching alone (increased batch sizes under same latency SLO): 10–25% unit cost savings for gen-heavy workloads.
- Prefix/KV cache (cache hit scenarios):
  - 0% cache hit: baseline costs above.
  - 30% cache hit: ~18–22% reduction in overall token spend.
  - 60% cache hit: ~35–45% reduction in overall token spend (depends on request distribution).

Quality / model parity notes\- For the POC we suggest comparing a Redwood-curated open model variant vs the comparable hyperscaler model (we’ll align on test prompts). In past POCs we’ve seen parity gaps around instruction-following; we’ll include an eval set in the run to score quality differences.

Proposed test plan (48h A/B)
1) Provision Redwood trial (hosted baseline + Dedicated trial node).
2) Run your sample workload through Redwood and through Bedrock/Azure endpoints with identical request timing and sample seeds.
3) Collect token counts, p50/p95 latency, and cache hit logs.
4) Produce a short report (cost delta, latency, quality diffs).

If that sounds good I can schedule the engineering sync Mon 10:30 PT — Marcus and Camila will join to set up the test harness.

Best,
Aditya

Attachment: redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx (updated, spreadsheet, 145KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 20:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive TCO & next tests

Jordan — quick note from engineering/solutions side. We can run the 48h controlled A/B and instrument token-level telemetry and cache stats. A couple of operational notes: 

- We’ll provision a short-lived Dedicated trial pool (no long-term commit required for the POC) and provide scoped API keys.
- For hyperscaler comparators, we’ll run against Bedrock + Azure OpenAI endpoints using the same inference drivers.
- We’ll include a small eval harness (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM evals) to capture quality deltas.

Next steps for procurement:
- I’ll send an NDA/POC engagement letter via DocuSign for the trial (covers data handling and audit requirements). Please sign so we can provision the trial node.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-ACME-TRIAL

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
